blueprint.definition: A detailed drawing that shows how a building should be made.

floor-plan.definition: A drawing showing the arrangement of rooms and features on one building level.

elevation.definition: A scaled drawing that shows one vertical face of a building as viewed straight on.

cross-section.definition: A drawing showing internal features as if an object or building had been cut through.

scale-model.definition: A physical representation whose dimensions have a stated proportion to the real object.

rendering.definition: A visual image that shows how an architectural design is expected to look.

sketch.definition: A quick simple drawing showing an idea or subject.

cad-software.definition: Computer software used to create precise technical drawings and designs.

3d-model.definition: A digital or physical representation showing an object's three dimensions.

site-plan.definition: A detailed drawing or map showing where buildings, driveways, utility lines, and other features are placed on a piece of land.

t-square.definition: A T-shaped ruler used to draw straight horizontal lines.

triangle.definition: A triangular drawing tool used to guide lines and angles.

compass.definition: A drawing instrument with two hinged arms used to draw circles or arcs.

protractor.definition: Drafting instrument used to draw or measure angles.
protractor.exampleUsage: Dina measures the angle with a protractor.

scale-ruler.definition: A ruler marked to measure distances on drawings made to scale.

drafting-table.definition: A sturdy worktable whose surface can be adjusted to different angles and heights.

tracing-paper.definition: A translucent sheet lets you see an image beneath it, so you can copy the image by following its lines.

pencil-set.definition: A collection of pencils with different grades for drawing and shading.

eraser-shield.definition: A thin sheet with openings that limits the area being erased.

french-curve.definition: A drawing tool with curved edges for making smooth irregular curves.

proportion.definition: The relationship between the sizes of parts in a design.

scale.definition: The fixed ratio between measurements on a drawing or model and the real object or building.

symmetry.definition: An arrangement in which parts correspond across a line, plane, or central point.

balance.definition: Harmonious arrangement or relation of parts or elements within a whole (as in a design).

rhythm.definition: The visual repetition or pattern of elements such as windows, columns, shapes, or spaces in a design.

contrast.definition: A noticeable difference between design elements, such as light and dark surfaces.

unity.definition: The sense that different parts of a design form a coherent whole.

emphasis.definition: Giving one design element greater visual prominence.

space.definition: An area or volume defined or organized within an architectural design.

form.definition: The three-dimensional shape and overall physical character of a building or object.

model-making-kit.definition: A set of tools and materials for building a small design model.

laser-cutter.definition: A machine that uses a focused laser beam to cut material precisely.

3d-printer.definition: A machine that creates three-dimensional objects from a digital model by building material layer by layer.
3d-printer.exampleUsage: The studio uses a 3D printer to produce the small building model.

light-table.definition: A table with a translucent top lit from below, used for tracing or examining drawings and images.
light-table.exampleUsage: The architect placed tracing paper on the light table.

pin-up-board.definition: A board used to display drawings, notes, plans, or images by attaching them with pins or tacks.
pin-up-board.exampleUsage: The team placed the latest sketches on the pin-up board.

material-samples.definition: Small pieces of materials kept so their color, texture, finish, or quality can be compared.
material-samples.exampleUsage: The architect compared several material samples before choosing the wall finish.

color-charts.definition: Organized sets of color samples used to compare and select exact shades.
color-charts.exampleUsage: The designer used color charts to choose a paint shade.

reference-books.definition: Books used mainly to look up reliable facts or specific information when needed.
reference-books.exampleUsage: The architect checked the reference books for standard dimensions.

projector.definition: A device that displays images on a wall or screen.
projector.exampleUsage: The projector displays the proposed facade on the wall.

plotter.definition: A machine used to produce large technical drawings or plans.
